seen_animation: A black-line boxy car in side profile, facing left, with a slanted windshield line and two rough polygon wheels, drives slowly leftward and away against grey scenery (a house roof outline, zigzag fence, trees, a vertical pole). Frames 1-4: the car is large, spanning almost the full panel width; its nose extends well left of the front wheel, which sits near the middle of the underside, and the rear wheel is small and squashed at the back corner. Frames 5-8: the car shrinks slightly, the front wheel moves toward the front, and the scenery slides right, bringing a large tree and pole in from the left. Frames 9-12: the car is smaller and positioned left of center, both wheels now near the ends of the body as in a plain side view; a small vehicle shape appears at the right edge in 9-10. Frames 13-16: the car keeps shrinking and stays at the lower left while trees, a pole, the house outline and a small square box sit behind and to the right of it.
seen_film: A white passenger van, seen from front three-quarters, starts large and close, filling most of the frame (1-4), with a house and bare trees behind. It drives left and away from the camera, turning toward a full side profile (5-8) while the camera pans so the house moves right. In 9-12 the van is in side profile, smaller, left of center, with tall trees and a pole behind it. In 13-16 it continues away, getting smaller at the lower left, with a white box and the house behind it to the right.
named_subject: A boxy van/car in side profile (the passenger van from the film)
evidence: Placement and scale track the film frame by frame: frame 1 car spans about x 10-360 of the panel versus the film van at about 25-370; frame 9 car sits left of center at about 40-320 like the film van in 9; frame 16 car spans about 60-240 at lower left versus the film van at about 50-250. Height shrinks steadily (about 180 px in 1, 165 in 5, 145 in 9, 110 in 12, 100 in 13, 78 in 16) with no sudden step, matching the film's recession. In frames 1-4 the front wheel sits near mid-underside and the nose runs forward of it, matching the film's three-quarter view where the front wheel is at about x 180; by frames 8-9 the wheels move to the body ends as the film van reaches side profile. Scenery pans right in step with the film: house outline moves right from 1 to 16, a tall tree and pole enter from the left by 5-9, and a small square box appears at lower right in 14-16 where the film's white box is. Judged from still frames only; playback was not seen.
primary_gap: In frames 1-4 the rear wheel is drawn as a small squashed shape hanging past the rear bottom corner (frame 4 it becomes a narrow vertical oval), unlike the round octagonal wheels under the body line in the doodle, and the wheel shapes change outline from frame to frame.
closes_when: The rear wheel in frames 1-4 is a full rough octagon of similar size to the front wheel, sitting under the body line just inside the rear corner, and both wheels keep the same outline across consecutive frames apart from scale.
protect: The single continuous body stroke with the slanted windshield and flat roof taken from the doodle; the steady shrink and leftward drift that matches the film's van position in every frame; the front wheel shifting from mid-underside (three-quarter view) to the front end (profile) across frames 1-9; the grey scenery panning right in step with the film; the thin, slightly broken line quality of the doodle.
identity_gap: The body stroke and wheel style match c.png, but in frames 1-4 the car is stretched long with a long nose ahead of the front wheel and a squashed rear wheel, so it looks less like the compact doodle until frame 8 onward.
